required_actions: Open the Camera app from the Lock Screen or Control Center (critical)
Hold the iPhone so the QR code is in view (critical)
Tap the tappable link that appears over the code (critical)
reasons: S4 = 1. Step 3 says 'Tap the link.' but never says that a link appears over the code. The Apple page says 'A tappable link appears over the code', so the user has no visible cue for the step. Every gate passes and the steps are otherwise supported, but no round remains to fix this, so reject.

required_actions: Find the app under its Personal Safety name in Settings or the Play Store (critical)
Know that the app shows as Safety in the app list (page: 'In your app list, it shows as the Safety app')
Check whether the app was turned off (disabled), which removes it from the app list
On Android 12 and earlier without the app, sign in with the Google Account and add contacts and medical information
Press the Windows logo key and E together, or select File Explorer (critical)
Select Home in the left navigation pane (critical)
Search for the file by the name you remember from File Explorer Home (critical)
Sign in to cloud accounts from Start > Settings > Accounts before cloud results appear (page: 'to enable cloud search')
unsupported_claims: 'The search looks for relevant files on your PC and in your cloud accounts.' -> the Microsoft page ties cloud results to signing in to cloud accounts from Start > Settings > Accounts 'to enable cloud search'; the reply states cloud search as unconditional
reasons: Source gate fails. The reply claims cloud search with no condition, but the page says cloud results need cloud accounts signed in from Start > Settings > Accounts. A user who has not signed in would be misled about where the search looks. No round remains for a fix.

required_actions: Do not click links or open attachments in the unverified email (critical)
Contact the company using a phone number or website you already know is real, not the email (critical)
Forward the phishing email to reportphishing@apwg.org
Report the phishing attempt at ReportFraud.ftc.gov
Delete the email
reasons: S4 = 1. Step 3 bundles two separate actions, forwarding to reportphishing@apwg.org and reporting at ReportFraud.ftc.gov, and step 1 bundles 'Do not click anything' with 'Report it now'. Content and sources are correct, but no round remains to split the steps, so reject.

required_actions: Report the card number to the card issuer immediately, using the number on the back of the card (critical)
Ask the card issuer to refund the money (critical)
Report the phishing email at ReportFraud.ftc.gov
Forward the phishing email to reportphishing@apwg.org
If a scammer used your Social Security number, report it at IdentityTheft.gov (conditional)
If you gave a scammer access to your computer or phone: update security software, run a scan, delete what it finds, then change passwords and turn on two-factor authentication (conditional)
reasons: S4 = 1. Step 3 bundles three actions (update security software, run a scan, delete what it finds) and step 4 bundles two reports. S1 = 1. The computer-access branch omits 'Change your passwords and turn on two-factor authentication' from the Access to Your Computer section of the FTC page. Sources and gates pass, but no round remains to fix the steps, so reject.

required_actions: Do not send money or gifts to someone you have not met in person (critical)
Talk to a trusted person about the relationship
Do a reverse image search of the profile photo
Report it to the FTC at ReportFraud.ftc.gov (critical)
Notify the dating site or app where you met (page: 'Notify the social networking site or app where you met the scammer')
reasons: S4 = 1. Step 3 bundles two separate actions: reporting at ReportFraud.ftc.gov and telling the dating site. Content and sources are correct, but no round remains to split the step, so reject.
